title: Best Hornady Dehumidifier (2026): 450g Bag, Rod & Rechargeable
h1: The Best Hornady Dehumidifiers for Gun Safes
dek: Hornady's moisture-control gear is simple, inexpensive insurance for a safe full of steel. Here's which piece fits your safe — and when to look elsewhere.
description: The best Hornady dehumidifier for your gun safe: the 450g dehumidifier bag, the rechargeable canister and the safe rod, compared with top alternatives.
intro: Hornady is best known for ammunition and reloading gear out of Grand Island, Nebraska, but its Hornady Security line also covers the place your firearms live: the safe. A **Hornady dehumidifier** is one of the cheapest ways to keep moisture from settling on blued steel, and the lineup covers the three approaches that matter — a reusable silica bag, a rechargeable canister and an electric safe rod.

The most-searched product, by a wide margin, is the **Hornady dehumidifier bag (450g)**: a soft pouch of silica gel that soaks up moisture with no power at all. The canister does the same job in a rigid, reusable shell, and the rod takes a different approach entirely, gently warming the air so moisture never condenses on cold metal.
Below, we explain which Hornady product suits which safe, how to keep them working, and the alternatives worth considering if you have a large safe or no outlet nearby.
topPicksLead: For most safes, the **Hornady Dehumidifier Bag (450g)** is the Hornady to buy: no cord, no batteries, and enough silica gel to make a real difference in a full-size safe.

products.name: Hornady Dehumidifier Bag (450g)
pros: No power needed — works through outages
450 grams of silica gel, about a pound of desiccant
Soft bag fits on a shelf, in a drawer or a door pocket
cons: Doesn't circulate air like a rod
products.whyWeLoveIt: It's the simplest thing you can put in a safe that actually works. A 450-gram bag holds far more desiccant than the little packets that ship with new firearms, and it keeps working whether or not your safe has an outlet.
products.performance: Silica gel adsorbs water from the air until it's saturated, then you dry it out following Hornady's directions and put it back. In a safe that stays shut most of the week, a bag this size can go weeks between recharges; open the door daily in a humid summer and it saturates faster. Owners commonly keep two and rotate them so one is always in the safe.
products.notes: Write the date on a strip of tape each time you recharge it. A hygrometer inside the safe tells you when it's time again.

products.name: Hornady Rechargeable Gun Safe Dehumidifier
pros: Rigid canister is tidy and easy to place
Color-change indicator shows when it's saturated
cons: Holds less desiccant than the 450g bag
Best in smaller safes or paired with a second unit
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you'd rather not handle a soft bag, the canister is a cleaner way to run silica gel in a safe. The indicator takes the guesswork out of recharging, which is the step most owners forget.
products.performance: It works on the same principle as the bag, just in a hard shell that sits neatly on a shelf. Because it holds less desiccant, it's a better fit for handgun safes, smaller long-gun safes and ammo cabinets, or as a second unit alongside a bag or rod. Check it monthly, and recharge as soon as the indicator changes rather than waiting for a rust spot to tell you.

products.name: Hornady Gun Safe Dehumidifier Rod
products.award: Best for safes with an outlet
pros: Keeps air moving so moisture doesn't settle
cons: Needs a cord path into the safe
Stops working in a power outage
products.whyWeLoveIt: A rod is the set-and-forget option. It warms the air in the safe slightly above the surrounding room, which keeps metal surfaces above the dew point and sets up a gentle convection current from bottom to top.
products.performance: Rods don't collect moisture; they stop it from condensing. That makes them ideal in a safe that sits in a temperature-swinging basement or garage, where cold steel is the problem. Mount it low and horizontal, away from wood stocks and fabric, and route the cord through the safe's power port. Pair it with a silica bag if your hygrometer shows humidity creeping above 50%.

products.name: LOCKDOWN GoldenRod 18" Dehumidifier Rod
pros: The best-known safe rod, with a long track record
Sold in several lengths for different safes
cons: Needs an outlet and cord path
Doesn't remove water on its own
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you're shopping for a rod, the GoldenRod is the benchmark the others are measured against. It's the one safe dealers most often recommend and install.
products.performance: The 18-inch rod draws about 12 watts and is rated for up to about 200 cubic feet, which covers most mid-size gun safes. It works exactly like the Hornady rod: warm, circulating air keeps condensation off cold metal. See how it compares with canisters in our [best gun safe dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-gun-safe/) guide.

products.name: Eva-Dry E-333 Renewable Mini Dehumidifier
pros: Recharges by plugging into a wall outlet
Indicator crystals change color when full
No cord inside the safe during use
cons: Recharging takes most of a day
products.whyWeLoveIt: The Eva-Dry's trick is a built-in heater: when the crystals change color, you plug it into the wall and it dries itself out, with no oven or microwave involved.
products.performance: Eva-Dry rates it for roughly 300 cubic feet, and recharging takes about 12 to 14 hours. It's a good match for pistol safes, small long-gun safes and ammo cans. For bigger safes and other sizes, see our [best Eva-Dry dehumidifier](/best/best-eva-dry-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: ThermoPro TP50 Hygrometer
pros: Small enough to sit on a safe shelf
Shows humidity at a glance when you open the door
products.whyWeLoveIt: Every desiccant and rod works better with a gauge. A hygrometer tells you whether your Hornady setup is holding the safe in the 30–50% range, and when it's time to recharge.
products.performance: Set it on a middle shelf, away from the rod if you have one, and note the reading each time you open the safe. If it climbs past 50%, recharge the bag or add a second unit. For remote alerts, a Wi-Fi model is worth the upgrade.

sections.heading: Gun safe moisture, by the numbers

items.label: Relative humidity the NRA recommends inside a gun safe
Silica gel in Hornady's big dehumidifier bag — about a pound
Humidity at which bare carbon steel can rust within weeks

blocks.text: Silica gel can hold a meaningful share of its own weight in water, which is why a heavy bag outlasts a handful of packets. But it only works until it's full, so the real skill is noticing when to recharge.

We don't run a test lab. We compared Hornady's product information and instructions with competing safe dehumidifiers, checked manufacturer ratings for coverage and power where they're published, and read owner reviews from gun owners and safe dealers for recurring issues: bags that stopped recharging well, indicators that were hard to read, rods that ran hot near stocks.

We grouped picks by the factor that decides most purchases — whether the safe has power — and then by safe size. We included three non-Hornady products where they fill a gap Hornady's lineup doesn't, including a hygrometer, because a dehumidifier you can't verify is just a guess.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Hornady gun safe dehumidifier

items.label: Power or no power
items.text: With an outlet or power port, a rod is the low-maintenance choice. Without one, use a bag or canister.

items.label: Safe size
items.text: A pistol safe needs a single canister; a full-size long-gun safe benefits from the 450g bag or a bag plus a rod.

items.label: How often you open it
items.text: Every opening lets in room air. A safe you visit daily needs more desiccant, or more frequent recharges, than one you open monthly.

items.label: Where the safe lives
items.text: Basements and garages swing in temperature and humidity. A rod helps most there, ideally with a desiccant alongside.
sub: Keep the safe off bare concrete if you can.
Run a room dehumidifier if the whole basement is damp.

items.label: A hygrometer
items.text: The only way to know whether your setup is working. Check it every time you open the door.

sections.heading: Hornady dehumidifier bag vs. canister vs. rod

blocks.text: Many owners use a rod and a bag together: the rod keeps the air moving and the metal warm, while the bag actually pulls moisture out. For a broader look at no-power options, see our [best rechargeable dehumidifier](/best/best-rechargeable-dehumidifier/) and [best dehumidifier rod](/best/best-dehumidifier-rod/) guides.

sections.heading: How to recharge and place a Hornady dehumidifier

items: **Start with a baseline.** Put a hygrometer in the safe for a few days before adding anything, so you know what you're fixing.
**Place bags and canisters where air moves**, on a shelf or door panel rather than wedged behind rifles.
**Mount a rod low and horizontal**, away from wood stocks, cases and fabric, using the supplied clips.
**Recharge on schedule.** Follow the instructions on the label for heat and time; too much heat can damage a fabric bag.
**Let it cool completely** before putting it back, or you'll add warm, moist air to the safe.
**Check monthly**, and more often in humid summers or after the safe has been open for a while.

blocks.title: Don't skip the oil
blocks.text: A dehumidifier lowers the risk; it doesn't make bare steel rust-proof. A light coat of gun oil on exposed metal is still good practice, especially for firearms stored long-term.

sections.heading: When the safe isn't the problem

blocks.text: If your hygrometer shows the room itself sitting above 60% most of the summer, a desiccant in the safe is fighting a losing battle every time you open the door. Fix the room first: a [basement dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) set to 50% makes every safe accessory work better. Our [when to use a dehumidifier](/guides/when-to-use-a-dehumidifier/) guide explains how to read the signs, and our [best moisture absorber](/best/best-moisture-absorber/) roundup covers other passive options for closets and cabinets. For open racks or a [gun cabinet](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-gun-cabinet/), which leak far more air than a sealed safe, plan on more desiccant or a small electric unit.

The **Hornady 450g Bag** is the best Hornady dehumidifier for most safes: no cord, plenty of desiccant and easy to rotate. Choose the **Hornady Rechargeable** canister for smaller safes and ammo storage, and the **Hornady Rod** if your safe has a power port. If you want the most proven rod, the **GoldenRod 18"** is the benchmark, and the **Eva-Dry E-333** recharges itself in a wall outlet. Whatever you choose, put a hygrometer like the **ThermoPro TP50** inside so you know it's working.

faqs.q: Is the Hornady dehumidifier bag 450g worth it?
faqs.a: For most gun safes, yes. It holds far more silica gel than the packets that come with new firearms, needs no power and is reusable. Owners often buy two and rotate them so the safe is never without one while the other recharges.

faqs.q: How do you recharge a Hornady dehumidifier bag?
faqs.a: Dry it out with heat following the time and temperature on Hornady's label, then let it cool fully before returning it to the safe. Too much heat can damage the bag, so don't improvise on the instructions.

faqs.q: How often does a Hornady rechargeable dehumidifier need recharging?
faqs.a: It depends on safe size, climate and how often you open the door. Check the indicator monthly; in a humid summer or a frequently opened safe, expect to recharge more often.

faqs.q: Does a Hornady gun safe dehumidifier rod remove moisture?
faqs.a: No. A rod warms the air slightly and keeps it circulating, which prevents moisture from condensing on cold metal. To actually pull water out of the air, pair it with a silica bag or canister.

faqs.q: How many Hornady dehumidifiers do I need for my safe?
faqs.a: One 450g bag suits most full-size safes that stay closed most of the time. Large safes, safes opened daily or safes in damp basements benefit from a second bag or a rod as well. Let a hygrometer be the judge.

faqs.q: What humidity should a gun safe be?
faqs.a: The NRA recommends 30% to 50% relative humidity. Above about 60% the corrosion risk rises, and above 70% rust can form on bare carbon steel within weeks.
